title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the functional student spaces and quiet corners of the College of Charleston that go beyond the standard historic highlights.

cards.title: Rivers Green
cards.subtitle: Outdoor study lawn behind Addlestone Library
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or snag a hammock for outdoor studying. It is a popular spot for sunbathing between classes with easy access to the library's Starbucks.
cards.short_summary: A large grassy area behind the main library used for outdoor studying and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: Rivers Green is described as a natural study spot where students bring textbooks to enjoy the sun, often using hammocks or patio furniture.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Students' Top 5 Study Spots in the Sun
cards.access_notes: Open public campus green space; best during daylight hours.

cards.title: Addlestone Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Designated silent study zone
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for absolute silence. Room 311 is specifically designated for silent study without a reservation for those needing deep focus.
cards.short_summary: The quietest floor of the main library, featuring silent study rooms and special collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor is designated for quiet study, with room 311 available for silent study without a reservation.
cards.source_title: Studying in Addlestone - College of Charleston Libraries
cards.access_notes: Requires Cougar Card for late-night access; visitors allowed 9am-5pm with ID.

cards.entity_name: Rita Liddy Hollings Science Center Roof Deck
cards.title: Hollings Science Center Roof Deck
cards.subtitle: Rooftop telescope and viewing area
cards.notes: Visit the fourth-floor roof for astronomy nights. It features telescope mounts and a viewing deck used by biology, physics, and astronomy students.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop facility at the science center used for astronomy labs and community viewing events.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth-floor roof houses an astronomy lab, telescope dome, and a publicly accessible roof deck for 'Astronomy Nights'.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Rita Hollings Science Center - HDR
cards.access_notes: Access typically during scheduled astronomy events or for science students.

cards.title: Halsey Institute of Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Contemporary art gallery in the Marion and Wayland H. Cato Jr. Center
cards.notes: Explore rotating contemporary exhibitions for free. The gallery is open until 7pm on Thursdays, making it a great late-afternoon cultural stop.
cards.short_summary: A non-collecting contemporary art museum on campus that hosts adventurous exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Halsey Institute is free and open to the public, with hours extending to 7pm on Thursdays during exhibitions.
cards.source_title: VISIT - Halsey Institute of Contemporary Art

cards.title: Stern Student Center Game Room
cards.subtitle: Student recreation and gaming hub
cards.notes: Located on the second floor, this space features video games and pool tables. It's a central spot for taking a break between classes.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated recreation area for students featuring gaming consoles and billiards.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stern Student Center includes a game room with video games and pool tables as part of its student life facilities.
cards.access_notes: Building undergoing renovations through late 2026; check current access for specific rooms.

cards.entity_name: School of Science and Mathematics Atrium
cards.title: SSMB Atrium
cards.subtitle: Study space with natural history displays
cards.notes: Study under pterodactyl skeletons and beside a fish tank. This quiet atrium offers tables and whiteboards on multiple floors for student use.
cards.short_summary: A bright, multi-story atrium in the science building used for quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Science and Mathematics building features a beautiful atrium with skeletons and fish tanks, plus study corners with whiteboards.
cards.source_title: Hitting the Books: Secret Study Spots
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; generally quieter than the library.

cards.title: Cougar Mall Fountain
cards.subtitle: Central campus meeting spot
cards.notes: Known by alumni as 'The Spot,' this fountain is a major intersection for meeting friends or professors between classes in Maybank Hall.
cards.short_summary: A central fountain and plaza area that serves as a primary social hub on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The fountain in Cougar Mall is described as a favorite meeting location for students and professors between classes.
cards.source_title: My Space: The Cougar Mall Fountain
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public plaza; non-amplified sound space.

cards.title: Avery Research Center
cards.subtitle: African American history and culture center
cards.notes: Visit for self-guided museum tours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. It preserves the unique history of the African diaspora in the Lowcountry.
cards.short_summary: A research center and museum dedicated to African American history and culture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Avery Research Center offers self-guided tours and houses archives available by appointment.
cards.access_notes: Museum tours Mon/Wed/Fri; Reading room by appointment only.

cards.title: Education Center 24/7 Space
cards.subtitle: Round-the-clock study location
cards.notes: A reliable 24/7 study spot for students when the library is closed. It is a favorite for late-night sessions and marathon studying.
cards.short_summary: An academic building known among students for providing 24-hour study access.
cards.evidence_claim: The Education Center is noted as a 24/7 study location for students.
cards.source_title: Favorite Study Locations at CofC – The Honor Roll
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 for students with valid ID.

cards.title: Cistern Yard
cards.subtitle: Historic green with live oaks
cards.notes: While iconic for graduation, students use this daily for 'cisternating'—socializing or studying under the Spanish moss-draped live oaks.
cards.short_summary: The historic heart of campus, used for both major ceremonies and daily student relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Cistern Yard serves as a gathering place for students to socialize and study, a practice historically called 'cisternating'.
cards.source_title: The CofC Cistern: More Than Meets the Eye
cards.access_notes: Open public campus space; often used for events.
